quest.title: Fauna Investigation Special Lecture
quest.description: There seems to be an event underway near Speranza...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x150, Primogem x20, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2

dialogues.speaker: Mikko
dialogues.text: As shiny as Mora, the Golden Loach King of the loachey world!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Mora? There's Mora?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And did Paimon just hear someone say something about gold...

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: You sure did! I discovered this uniquely colored Golden Loach while exploring up north. It was the only one in the area with such a distinctive color.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: It's thriving now, and I've had a doctor who knows about animals take a look. The color doesn't seem to be caused by anything pathological.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then why does it look so different?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: It could be any number of things. Habitat, environment, the characteristics of the water it lives in, climate... even its diet.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: But if you're asking me to pin it down to one specific reason, I'm afraid I just don't know.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And not knowing doesn't bother you?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Why would it? It's such a rare phenomenon, I'm incredibly lucky just to have witnessed it.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Being able to document my discovery, draw inferences, and make conjectures is more than enough for me!

dialogues.speaker: Maisie
dialogues.text: It's just like a Pink Frostfin Whale...

dialogues.speaker: Maisie
dialogues.text: They say if you get the chance to see a Pink Frostfin Whale, your wishes will come true — but they're super, duper rare.

dialogues.speaker: Maisie
dialogues.text: Even so, we saw one once, when we were with Linnea. I think it was because she brought us good luck.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, we should go look for one too! Paimon has so many wishes... Which one should the whale grant first?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do different colors really give them mystical powers...?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: ...It's probably just wishful thinking.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So pink whales don't have mystical powers!?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Well, there are some examples of some creatures with special colors possessing unique abilities... but the Frostfin Whale we saw probably wasn't one of them.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: If people were just making wishes, that would be one thing... I'm just worried someone might hurt it because they believe those fanciful stories.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Would people really do that?

dialogues.speaker: Mikko
dialogues.text: I know this one! Katya told me that some really nasty treasure hunters hunt animals with unusual colors to sell them to collectors.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: That's right. There was a time when animals from Natlan were highly prized on the black market — live specimens in particular, but bones and furs would also fetch a high price.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Some merchants, looking to sell their smuggled goods at inflated prices, would even go so far as to process and alter them, packaging them as some kind of "fantasy" product before selling them to customers.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: There was a case I heard where poachers removed the feet from Qucusaurs to make them more aesthetically pleasing and easier to transport...

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Collectors who'd never seen a Qucusaurus before actually thought they were naturally legless, spending their entire lives soaring through the sky, living off wind and dew... like some kind of marvel of nature.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Their reckless pursuit of the exotic only fueled the poachers' wickedness — they created a whole smuggling network born from greed and deceit, causing untold harm and suffering...

dialogues.speaker: Lumi
dialogues.text: Ya-ho...

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: In a sea of evil deeds, even a relatively minor act, such as dyeing a creature to change its color, is still wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Maisie
dialogues.text: S—So... should we give that Silver Capybara a bath? Was it also dyed this color by nasty poachers?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: I don't think that'll be necessary. When I found it, it was taking a soak in a Hilichurl's cooking pot. Maybe it thought it was a hot spring?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: There can't be that many born with fur like that. That's probably why the smugglers took it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon can totally imagine what it must have looked like in that cooking pot...

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Right? Despite its unique color, it still has the same nature and temperament as other Capybaras.

dialogues.speaker: Mikko
dialogues.text: Come to think of it, we caught a White Weasel Thief once before, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Mora thief! What happened to it in the end?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: We let it go. Hopefully it's learned its lesson and won't go near any more Fatui research facilities...

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Unlike our Capybara friend, its change in color must be an acquired trait — perhaps a result of being exposed to such high concentrations of kuuvahki.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That makes sense...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: When Paimon thinks about it like that, it seems being unique isn't always a good thing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Just thinking about how some creatures might suffer because they're different, or that the only reason they're different is that something bad happened to make them that way...

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: It might sound a little selfish, but if Lumi wasn't such a special little Jack Frost, we might never have become partners to begin with...

dialogues.speaker: Lumi
dialogues.text: Ya-ho! Ya-hoho!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It doesn't seem to mind.

dialogues.speaker: Mikko
dialogues.text: So it's not always a bad thing either?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If being different brought the two of you together, then of course it's a good thing!

dialogues.speaker: Mikko
dialogues.text: I remember Helka mentioning a saying from Liyue in one of her letters, something about blessings and misfortune...

dialogues.speaker: Maisie
dialogues.text: "Every misfortune conceals a blessing, and every blessing hides misfortune."

dialogues.speaker: Mikko
dialogues.text: Hehe, that's the one! By the way, Ms. Linnea, you're being awfully quiet. Where's all that teacher energy gone?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: I never thought I'd see the day when you'd be calling me out, Mikko...

dialogues.speaker: Mikko
dialogues.text: W—Well, you were once part of the Conch Gang too, Ms. Linnea! *sigh* Anyway, why don't we just drop all this deep stuff for today, and you can tell us about the Volkodlak!

dialogues.speaker: Mikko
dialogues.text: Are they really that strong? How do they compare to Snegovik and Leshy?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Hmm, there are many fascinating stories about the Volkodlak that I could tell you... but they'll have to wait for next time.

dialogues.speaker: Mikko
dialogues.text: Ugh, not "next time" again... Alright, but you'd better remember!

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Sorry for making you sit through that...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't be. I learned quite a few things today too.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Seriously? That's wonderful...

dialogues.speaker: Mikko
dialogues.text: Hey, I just realized something — you all went to see that Frostfin Whale without me!

dialogues.speaker: Maisie
dialogues.text: You were the one who overslept!

dialogues.speaker: Mikko
dialogues.text: Huh? I—In that case, make sure to wake me up next time...
